edges.description: The K392R knock-in develops progressive lymphoid hyperplasia and systemic inflammation with Th17 expansion.
edges.limitations: Shows Th17 and effector-T expansion without the overt Treg dysfunction inferred from some human data, so it informs the effector arm more than the regulatory arm.

edges.description: The G421R knock-in reproduces T-cell dysregulation and lymphoproliferation but with largely intact Treg numbers and function, isolating the lesion to induced-Treg generation.
edges.limitations: Core Treg function is preserved in the model, so it does not reproduce a primary Treg-suppression defect; the human relevance of the induced-Treg deficiency is still being defined.

nodes.description: Autoimmune cytopenias, spanning immune thrombocytopenia, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, and autoimmune neutropenia, are among the most frequent manifestations. Bound to the lineage-agnostic Autoimmune cytopenia term so the binding is no narrower than the multi-lineage claim.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Aspects of STAT3 Gain-of-Function Germline Mutations: A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: The most frequent manifestations were autoimmune cytopenias (28 of 42)

nodes.description: Autoimmune enteropathy presenting with chronic diarrhea and failure to thrive; bound to the chronic-diarrhea phenotype as HPO has no exact autoimmune-enteropathy term.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Aspects of STAT3 Gain-of-Function Germline Mutations: A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: lymphoproliferation (27 of 42), enteropathy (24 of 42)

nodes.description: Autoimmune hepatitis occurs in a substantial minority of patients.

evidence.reference_title: Monogenic early-onset lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity: Natural history of STAT3 gain-of-function syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Autoimmune hepatitis occurred in 14% of patients.

nodes.description: Interstitial lung disease is a frequent and sometimes fatal manifestation, ranging from interstitial pneumonitis to fibrotic and cystic tissue destruction.

evidence.reference_title: Early-onset, fatal interstitial lung disease in STAT3 gain-of-function patients.
evidence.snippet: Here we report three individuals with de-novo STAT3 GOF alleles and early-onset, severe interstitial lung disease manifesting during the first 3 years of life.

nodes.description: Autoimmune thyroid disease, usually presenting as hypothyroidism.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Aspects of STAT3 Gain-of-Function Germline Mutations: A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: thyroiditis (13 of 42), diabetes (10 of 42)

nodes.description: STAT3 is the shared transcription factor of many cytokine receptors. GOF variants produce sustained STAT3 phosphorylation, nuclear translocation, and increased target-gene transcription that is not appropriately restrained, amplifying the cytokine-driven transcriptional program and secondarily dampening STAT5- and STAT1-dependent signals.

evidence.reference_title: Jakinibs for the treatment of immune dysregulation in patients with gain-of-function signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) or STAT3 mutations.
evidence.snippet: STAT molecules are then recruited to the activated receptor, are phosphorylated, dimerize, and translocate to the nucleus where they alter gene expression.

nodes.description: GOF STAT3 drives oligoclonal accumulation of effector CD8+ T cells that highly express NKG2D and cytotoxic effector genes. In mice, these cells are necessary for lethal autoimmune pathology, and in humans the same expansion links the syndrome to large granular lymphocytic leukemia.
nodes.id: Effector CD8+ T Cell Clonal Accumulation

evidence.reference_title: STAT3 gain-of-function mutations connect leukemia with autoimmune disease by pathological NKG2D(hi) CD8(+) T cell dysregulation and accumulation.
evidence.snippet: Leukocyte-restricted STAT3 GOF was sufficient and CD8+ T cells were essential for lethal pathology in mice.

evidence.reference_title: STAT3 gain-of-function mutations connect leukemia with autoimmune disease by pathological NKG2D(hi) CD8(+) T cell dysregulation and accumulation.
evidence.snippet: To investigate whether these mutations are the cause or consequence of CD8+ T cell clonal expansions and autoimmunity, we analyzed patients and mice with germline STAT3 GOF mutations.

nodes.description: Postnatal growth failure is a prominent non-immune feature. Chronic inflammation and possible direct effects of excess STAT3 activity on the growth-hormone signaling pathway are implicated, though the precise intermediates remain unresolved.

evidence.reference_title: Activating mutations of STAT3: Impact on human growth.
evidence.snippet: short stature is a predominant feature in this condition

evidence.reference_title: Monogenic early-onset lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity: Natural history of STAT3 gain-of-function syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Growth failure was observed in more than half of patients, raising concern for defects in growth hormone signaling, which requires STAT5b.

nodes.description: STAT3 is required for the transition of classical CD14+ monocytes into the CD16+ nonclassical subset and for CD141+ dendritic-cell development. GOF patients show a selective deficiency of these populations plus hypogammaglobulinemia with terminal B-cell maturation arrest, contributing to susceptibility to infection.
nodes.id: Impaired Nonclassical Monocyte and Dendritic Cell Development

evidence.reference_title: STAT3 Gain-of-Function Mutations Underlie Deficiency in Human Nonclassical CD16(+) Monocytes and CD141(+) Dendritic Cells.
evidence.snippet: This suggests a role for STAT3 in the transition of classical CD14+ monocytes into the CD16+ nonclassical subset.

nodes.description: Janus kinase inhibitors (ruxolitinib and other jakinibs) block the kinase step upstream of the constitutively active STAT3 and dramatically improve clinical, immunologic, and transcriptomic abnormalities. They are the most consistently effective targeted therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Monogenic early-onset lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity: Natural history of STAT3 gain-of-function syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Clinical symptoms dramatically improved in patients treated with JAK inhibitors, while a variety of other immunomodulatory treatment modalities were less efficacious.

nodes.description: The combined reduction of regulatory T cells and expansion of autoreactive effector T cells breaks peripheral tolerance, producing autoimmunity across many organs: hematologic (autoimmune cytopenias), gastrointestinal (enteropathy), endocrine (thyroiditis, type 1 diabetes), pulmonary (interstitial lung disease), and hepatic (autoimmune hepatitis).
nodes.id: Loss of Immune Tolerance and Multiorgan Autoimmunity

evidence.reference_title: Activating germline mutations in STAT3 cause early-onset multi-organ autoimmune disease.
evidence.snippet: These findings emphasize the critical role of STAT3 in autoimmune disease

evidence.reference_title: Monogenic early-onset lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity: Natural history of STAT3 gain-of-function syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Seventy-three percent of patients had evidence of lymphoproliferation most commonly manifesting as diffuse lymphadenopathy (75.5%) and/or splenomegaly (72%).

nodes.description: Accumulation of expanded lymphocyte clones produces non-malignant lymphoproliferation: lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly, the most common manifestations of the syndrome, with an increased risk of lymphoid malignancy (including large granular lymphocytic leukemia).

evidence.reference_title: Monogenic early-onset lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity: Natural history of STAT3 gain-of-function syndrome.
evidence.snippet: lymphoproliferation was the most common manifestation (73%)

evidence.reference_title: Monogenic early-onset lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity: Natural history of STAT3 gain-of-function syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Malignancy occurred in 12 patients

nodes.description: Autoimmune arthritis, characterized as polyarticular, affects a minority of patients.

evidence.reference_title: Monogenic early-onset lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity: Natural history of STAT3 gain-of-function syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Eighteen percent of patients developed arthritis that was characterized as polyarticular.

nodes.description: Recurrent infections reflect the immunodeficiency arm of the disease, including hypogammaglobulinemia and impaired myeloid/dendritic development.

evidence.reference_title: Monogenic early-onset lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity: Natural history of STAT3 gain-of-function syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Infections were reported in 72% of the cohort.

nodes.description: Constitutive STAT3 activity, acting in part through reduced STAT5 signaling, lowers regulatory T-cell numbers and impairs induced-Treg generation, weakening peripheral tolerance. Mouse models suggest the dominant lesion is effector-cell expansion rather than loss of Treg suppressive function, so the reduction is in the numeric/inducible compartment rather than in core Treg function.

animal_models.name: STAT3 G421R knock-in mouse

evidence.reference_title: A human STAT3 gain-of-function variant confers T cell dysregulation without predominant Treg dysfunction in mice.
evidence.snippet: Treg numbers, phenotype, and function remained largely intact; however, mice had a selective deficiency in the generation of iTregs

nodes.description: Germline heterozygous missense variants in STAT3, clustered in the DNA-binding and dimerization domains (e.g. p.K392R, p.M394T, p.K658N), confer a gain of function. The mutant transcription factor shows increased DNA-binding activity and a preference for the active, nuclear-localized state.

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmunity, hypogammaglobulinemia, lymphoproliferation, and mycobacterial disease in patients with activating mutations in STAT3.
evidence.snippet: 3 patients with de novo activating mutations in the DNA binding or dimerization domains of STAT3 (p.K392R, p.M394T, and p.K658N, respectively)

nodes.description: Postnatal growth failure and short stature are prominent and frequent non-immune features.

evidence.snippet: postnatal growth failure (15 of 21)

nodes.description: Skin lesions are common, most often eczematoid dermatitis; the Th17-driven skin inflammation of the mouse models has a human counterpart here.

evidence.snippet: Forty-eight percent of patients had skin lesions, with eczema (60%), psoriasis (12%), and alopecia (10%) being the most common findings.

evidence.reference_title: Monogenic early-onset lymphoproliferation and autoimmunity: Natural history of STAT3 gain-of-function syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Seventy-three percent of patients had evidence of lymphoproliferation most commonly manifesting as diffuse lymphadenopathy (75.5%) and/or splenomegaly (72%).

nodes.description: Elevated STAT3 activity favors Th17 differentiation; tissue-restricted Th17 responses contribute to organ-specific inflammation such as skin disease.

evidence.reference_title: A human STAT3 gain-of-function variant drives local Th17 dysregulation and skin inflammation in mice.
evidence.snippet: We observed spontaneous and imiquimod (IMQ)-induced skin inflammation associated with cell-intrinsic local Th17 responses in STAT3 GOF mice.
